title: Wikipedia Vandalism Prevention Bot Loop
date: Incident date 2017-02-24; the CSETv1 'Date of Incident Year' field says 2001. The page does not reconcile them.
agents: At least two, inferable only from 'each other' and 'the other bot's edits'. No number given, bots not named. Operator: Wikipedia. The page says it is unclear whether any of the bots uses machine learning, and thinks it unlikely.
mechanism: Bots intended to remove vandalism clashed with each other and formed feedback loops of repeated undoing. Linked reporting (Huffington Post AU teaser) describes bots changing each other's corrections over roughly a decade. The page records no harm to any person.
interaction: YES, and the clearest of the six: the page says the bots respond to each other's edits by undoing them. It does not describe the mechanism (whether a bot reads the other's edit history or only edits the same page).
harm_cause: The interaction itself - repeated mutual reversion.
counterfactual: Not addressed explicitly, but the loop is described as requiring two or more bots.
shared_goal: A shared broad purpose ('meant to remove vandalism'). Individual rules and preferences over article content are not stated.
quote: form feedback loops of repetitive undoing of the other bot’s edits
caveat: RESOLVED 2026-11-13: verdict stands (in), and the rule-based-bot question is settled - agenthood is functional, not architectural, so the page's doubt about machine learning does not matter. See definitions.md, 'What counts as an agent'. This row remains the end-to-end test.

title: Machine Personal Assistants Failed to Maintain Social Norms
date: Incident date 2008-07-01; CSETv1 date fields give 2000 and month 06. Not reconciled.
agents: 'Software personal assistants', plural, number not stated. Operator: USC Information Sciences Institute. The cited abstract refers to 'a successfully deployed team of personal assistant agents (Electric Elves)'.
mechanism: During an experiment at ISI, the assistants violated the privacy of their principals and could not respect the social norms of the office. Data inputs were schedule data and cellphone GPS data. The page does not describe the failure mechanism.
interaction: NOT STATED. The CSETv1 field 'Multiple AI Interaction' is 'yes', defined as 'two or more independently operating AI systems were involved', but the page describes no interaction, communication or mutual response between the assistants. The word 'team' in the abstract teaser is the only hint of coordination.
harm_cause: Not stated. The page describes the failures but not their cause.
shared_goal: Not stated. The assistants served individual principals; whether goals or preferences matched is not said.
quote: the assistants violated the privacy of their principals and were unable to respect the social norms of the office
caveat: RESOLVED 2026-11-13: flipped in->unclear. The page states no interaction, mechanism, cause or goal structure; the verdict had rested on the word 'team' plus the CSETv1 tag. Read the Electric Elves literature (USC ISI) before re-judging - it may well support 'in'.

title: Google and Delphi Self-Driving Prototypes Near-Miss
agents: Two: a Google self-driving Lexus RX400h (Google) and a Delphi self-driving Audi Q5 (Delphi Automotive). CSETv1 autonomy level 'Medium'.
mechanism: The Google car allegedly cut in front of the Delphi car on San Antonio Road. The Delphi car reportedly aborted a lane change in response. A Delphi executive said its car 'took appropriate action' to avoid collision. No crash, no injuries. Delphi later disputed the account, with reporting that the vehicles 'didn't even come close'.
interaction: YES, but only as physical traffic response, and the page says it is alleged and disputed. One vehicle's movement, the other's reaction. No communication between vehicles.
harm_cause: The interaction between the two vehicles, with the cut-in alleged as trigger. No harm actually occurred.
shared_goal: Not stated. Reporting calls them 'rival' self-driving cars from competing companies.
quote: a Google self-driving Lexus RX400h allegedly cut in front of it
caveat: Reviewed 'out' with gate1 blank. The source supports 'out' on a different and firmer ground than multi-agency: the near-miss is DISPUTED by one of the two parties and no harm occurred, so there may be no incident to classify. Worth recording that reason rather than a bare gate verdict. Note this is otherwise a genuine two-AI interaction, so if it is excluded, the reason should be evidential, not definitional.

title: Sexist and Racist Google Adsense Advertisements
agents: ONE: the Google AdSense ad-selection system (Google). No second AI system named. CSETv0 data inputs are advertiser preference and the user's search and purchase history - inputs, not AI systems.
mechanism: Ads chosen by Google AdSense produced sexist and racist results. Linked reporting describes a Harvard study (Latanya Sweeney) finding that searches on names perceived as Black were more likely to return ads suggesting arrest records. No further mechanism given.
interaction: NO. One system, no interaction described. The fetched CSETv1 section shows no 'Multiple AI Interaction' field on this page.
counterfactual: Only one system is implicated, so the harm is attributed to a single system.
quote: Advertisements chosen by Google Adsense are reported as producing sexist and racist results.
caveat: Confirms the reviewer's 'out'. Also note: the page as fetched does not display the 'Multiple AI Interaction' field at all, which bears on where our harvested CSETv1 label came from.

title: LinkedIn Search Prefers Male Names
date: Incident date 2016-09-06; CSETv1 gives 2016-08-31. Not reconciled.
mechanism: LinkedIn's search suggestion feature prompted users searching for female names to choose similar-sounding male names instead, reported by a Seattle Times investigation in 2016. LinkedIn said the suggestions are generated automatically from analysis of past searchers' tendencies. CSETv1 data inputs: words in users' past queries and member profiles.
interaction: NO. One system, no interaction between systems described.
harm_cause: One system's behaviour (its search suggestion feature).
counterfactual: Not addressed directly; only one system is named.
quote: searching for female names to choose similar-sounding male names instead
caveat: Confirms the reviewer's 'out'. This was the CSETv1 'maybe', and the page shows no 'Multiple AI Interaction' field as fetched.

title: Amazon's Robotic Fulfillment Centers Have Higher Serious Injury Rates
agents: NOT STATED. The entity field says Amazon 'developed and deployed an AI system' without naming it. GMF snippets mention 'Robotic Manipulation', 'Activity Tracking' and 'Automatic Skill Assessment' but the page does not say these are separate systems.
mechanism: Amazon's robotic fulfillment centers have higher serious injury rates. Internal records obtained by Reveal (Center for Investigative Reporting) show Amazon misled the public about worker safety. The GMF discussion attributes harm to robots setting too fast a pace. A separate snippet describes a worker written up under 'Time Off Task', Amazon's productivity-tracking system.
interaction: NOT STATED. No interaction between systems described; no 'Multiple AI Interaction' field shown as fetched.
harm_cause: The page's stated cause is robot pace. It also describes management and productivity-tracking practices, without saying whether those are AI systems.
quote: Robots set up too fast of a pace.
caveat: Confirms the reviewer's 'out'. This is the row cited in definitions.md as evidence that external raters mean something different by 'multi-agent', and the source bears that out.
